title: bug: waitForGuestReady owner check passes any seat owner on a seat record
description: scripts/local-runner/guest-readiness.mjs:252 compares only owner.taskId/attemptId/generation with the record's. On a CQ-M07g seat record all three are undefined on both sides, so ANY seat owner (or {}) passes the LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER check. Today provisionGuest calls it right after provisionOwned's sameOwner check, so the impact is defense-in-depth only. Fix: use lifecycle's owner comparison (sameOwner semantics, seat keys for seat records), plus a row where a foreign seat owner is refused. Found in CQ-M07i (task-18809c69).
definitionOfDone: waitForGuestReady refuses LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER for a seat record whose owner differs in workerId, runner or host, and for an attempt owner on a seat record (rows).
Attempt-record behavior is unchanged (existing readiness rows green in a git-archive snapshot).

implementationPlan.description:
Write the seat-record readiness test rows first, then make them pass by reusing lifecycle's owner comparison. Use the main session's Edit tool for all three files (rail: no shell writes to tracked files). Read mem:gotcha-local-runner-tests first (sections 'running scripts/tests/local-runner*.test.mjs on a clean git-archive export' and 'CQ-M07g task-9076afab').

(a) Test, scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs. Directly after the test 'readiness is refused before any provider call unless the caller owns an owned record' (it ends with `assert.equal((await ledger.read(nameAt(6))).image, undefined);` and `});`), add a module-level `const SEAT = Object.freeze({ workerId: 'worker-a1', runner: '4242@tok a', host: 'host-a' });` (this file has no SEAT identifier yet) and ONE new test named 'GR-S1 readiness on a seat record refuses a foreign seat owner or an attempt owner before any provider call; its own seat owner boots it'. It reuses only existing helpers: scratch, createLedger, sequence, seed, GUEST, fakeGuest, SOURCE, BOOTSTRAP, noSleep, owner, assertSanitized, bootGuest, outcome, PROVIDER_HASH, readFileSync, path. The architect prototyped this body in a git-archive snapshot:
- `const dir = scratch(t); const ledger = createLedger(dir, { random: sequence() });`
- `assert.equal((await seed(ledger, 'owned', 1, SEAT)).instance, GUEST);` (the first reserve on sequence() is nameAt(1) = GUEST; reserve writes a seat record for a seat owner) and `const attempt = await seed(ledger, 'owned');` (nameAt(2), an attempt record).
- `const file = path.join(dir, `${GUEST}.json`); const before = readFileSync(file); const fake = fakeGuest();`
- `const call = (name, who) => waitForGuestReady({ ledger, name, owner: who, sourceImage: SOURCE, bootstrap: BOOTSTRAP, provider: { run: fake.run }, sleep: noSleep });`
- labelled rows, each `await assert.rejects(call(GUEST, who), error => assertSanitized(error, 'LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER'), label)`: 'another workerId' { ...SEAT, workerId: 'worker-b2' }, 'another runner' { ...SEAT, runner: '4343@tok a' }, 'another host' { ...SEAT, host: 'host-b' }, 'an attempt owner' owner, 'an empty owner' {}, 'no owner' undefined, 'a null owner' null. Then `call(attempt.instance, SEAT)` must also reject LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER ('a seat owner on an attempt record').
- `assert.equal(fake.calls.length, 0);` (every refusal comes before any provider call) and `assert.deepEqual(readFileSync(file), before);` (no ledger write).
- positive control: `const run = await bootGuest({ ledger }, {}, { owner: SEAT }); assert.deepEqual(run.result, outcome([])); assert.deepEqual((await ledger.read(GUEST)).image, { sourceSha256: SOURCE.sha256, providerImageHash: PROVIDER_HASH });`. The matching seat owner must still boot its own seat VM (CQ-M07i's seat start reaches this through provisionGuest), so a fix that refused every seat record fails here.
Against the unchanged runtime GR-S1 is RED with 'Missing expected rejection: another workerId' (today a foreign seat owner boots the guest and records the image). The architect observed this; re-running RED is optional.

(b) Fix. scripts/local-runner/lifecycle.mjs:150: change `const sameOwner =` to `export const sameOwner =` and leave the body byte-identical. Add a one-line comment saying it is the single owner comparison every ledger reader uses: a seat record by workerId, runner and host; an attempt record by taskId, attemptId and generation. scripts/local-runner/guest-readiness.mjs: add sameOwner to the existing './lifecycle.mjs' import, keeping alphabetical order (invoker, lifecycleError, QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS, sameOwner, STATES). In waitForGuestReady, replace the three-line `if (owner?.taskId !== record.taskId || owner?.attemptId !== ... ) { throw lifecycleError('LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER'); }` block with `if (!sameOwner(record, owner)) throw lifecycleError('LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER');`. Keep the order: validInputs, pinnedSource, invoker, ledger.read, owner check, phase check.

Error handling: the refusal stays the existing sanitized lifecycleError (code only, no diagnostics), thrown before any provider call or ledger write. sameOwner reads `owner?.[key]`, so a null, undefined or {} owner is refused, never a TypeError. Do not add owner-shape validation (validOwner/validSeatOwner) or a new error code. The contract is sameOwner semantics, exactly as provisionOwned and deleteOwned already apply them. Attempt records keep identical semantics: ATTEMPT_KEYS is taskId, attemptId and generation with strict equality, the same three comparisons the removed block made. So every existing readiness test row stays unchanged and green (DoD 2).
implementationPlan.note: Added GR-S1 + SEAT; exported sameOwner (comment only); waitForGuestReady uses sameOwner. Other dirty paths belong to peers, untouched.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: waitForGuestReady accepts exactly the owner lifecycle's sameOwner accepts. On a CQ-M07g seat record, that is only an owner whose workerId, runner and host all equal the record's. On an attempt record, it is only an owner whose taskId, attemptId and generation equal the record's. Any other owner gets LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER before any provider call or ledger write: a foreign seat owner, an attempt owner on a seat record, a seat owner on an attempt record, {}, null or undefined.
acceptanceCriteria: GR-S1 refuses LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER on a seat record for another workerId, runner or host, an attempt owner, {}, undefined and null, and for a seat owner on an attempt record. It makes zero provider calls and leaves the record bytes unchanged.
GR-S1's positive control: the matching seat owner boots the guest (outcome([])), and the image is recorded on the seat record.
Every pre-existing test in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs and scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs passes unchanged in the git-archive snapshot gate.

The owner check precedes the phase check and every provider call

provisionOwned, deleteOwned and retireRecord keep the same sameOwner

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Export lifecycle.mjs sameOwner and call it from waitForGuestReady. Chosen: one owner comparison for every ledger reader, as the task asks, and a one-keyword change to lifecycle.mjs. (2) Re-implement the seat/attempt key choice inside guest-readiness.mjs with isSeatRecord. Rejected: a second copy of SEAT_OWNER_KEYS/ATTEMPT_KEYS that can drift. (3) A new assertOwner helper in lifecycle.mjs adopted by provisionOwned and deleteOwned too. Rejected: wider diff, no behavior gain (ponytail). (4) Validate owner shape up front as BOOTSTRAP_INPUT_INVALID. Rejected: it changes the refusal code that the existing rows pin for null/undefined owners on attempt records.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: lifecycle.mjs:150 `const sameOwner = (record, owner) => (isSeatRecord(record) ? SEAT_OWNER_KEYS : ATTEMPT_KEYS).every(key => owner?.[key] === record[key])` is module-private. provisionOwned (342), deleteOwned (483) and retireRecord (298) use it. guest-readiness.mjs:252 compares only taskId/attemptId/generation. On a seat record all three are undefined, so any seat owner, {} or undefined passes. ledger.reserve writes a seat record (workerId, runner, host, platform=process.platform) for a validSeatOwner owner, so the test fixture seed(ledger, 'owned', 1, SEAT) works unchanged. The seat test file injects a fake provision, so before GR-S1 no test drove waitForGuestReady with a seat owner. Architect prototype in a git-archive snapshot: GR-S1 RED on HEAD runtime; GREEN with the fix; 6/6 probe mutants killed (swapped sameOwner args, refuse-every-seat, old inline check, each seat key dropped); full two-file gate 407/406/0 fail/1 skip.
planningNotes.risks: No open task declares these three files (checked across all 34 open rows), so landing is uncontested. The positive control matters most: a fix that refused every seat record would break CQ-M07i seat start via provisionGuest, and only GR-S1's bootGuest row catches that. The test is platform-neutral: temp ledger, fake provider, and process.platform is a valid record platform on win32/darwin/linux; CI runs this file on all three OSes. Mid-epic bug row: the narrow gate is enough; the epic-final row owns full regression.
